newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to act in case of excessive forex moves - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to act in case of excessive forex moves - MOF.

text.p: Japan will continue to act appropriately to deal with excessive movements in foreign exchange markets, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa said on Monday.
"This is generally speaking but we will continue to deal appropriately with excessive moves while keeping close watch (over the forex market)," he said.

He also said that stable currency markets were important for Japan's economy. "Excessive weakness of the yen, as the same with excessive strength of the yen, is certainly not favourable for the economy," he said.
He said the government was watching market movements "with great interest" as they were one of the many indicators which show the state of the Japanese economy.
Asked about the state of Japan's economy, Ogawa said that economic conditions were becoming firmer.
"There is no change in my view that the economic cycle is becoming firmer," Ogawa said.

Asked about how much supervisory powers MOF should have over the Bank of Japan, Ogawa said there was a need for the government to have some kind of supervisory function to see whether the central bank was functioning properly for the good of the public and the economy.
However, this did not necessarily mean the government should interfere in the BOJ's daily business, he said.
